newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's SAA locks out protesting workers.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's SAA locks out protesting workers.

text.p: South African Airways (SAA) said on Wednesday it had locked out about 1,800 aviation technicians and engineers nationwide for failing to end a work-to-rule protest they began last week.
"SAA has instituted the lock-out procedure at all airports throughout the country," SAA spokeswoman Zelda Schuulabach said.
The lock-out was enforced after management and union members could not reach a settlement on wage increases at a meeting on Tuesday.
But Schuulabach added that about a quarter of the 2,200-strong South African Aviation Engineering and Allied Union (SAAEAU) had reported for work.
All domestic and international flight schedules would be affected in varying degrees by the lock-out, Schuulabach said.
"Trying to get domestic flights to their destinations could see delays of up to an hour. No doubt there will be delays on international flights," she said.
Domestic and international flights at Johannesburg airport have been disrupted since SAAEAU began their action on Wednesday last week.
SAA would monitor the situation, re-routing and re-scheduling flights where necessary, Schuulabach said.
She advised passengers who did not need to travel to postpone their flights.
Last week two flights to London and Miami from Johannesburg, which serves as SAA's technical operations hub, were delayed for about 15 hours overnight -- leaving hundreds of passengers stranded.

SAAEAU has declared a dispute with SAA for its refusal to offer a 25 percent wage rise. Schuulabach said management was willing to continue the mediation process but would not further discuss the requested pay hike.
